A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SSFL despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, revised and added material.

before.justification: V1 reports original federated classification experiments, mask analyses and geographically distributed communication-time measurements in Section 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds ResNet-50, oracle-mask estimation, warmup and distribution-shift results in Section 4 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: V2 adds one-shot OOD adaptation: clients recompute saliency using trained active weights and original initializations for inactive weights, then refresh the shared mask and resume training (Section 4.3, Algorithm 2). This substantially extends v1's fixed-mask procedure. The stated Algorithm 1 also changes initialization from averaging client initializations to server initialization, and model aggregation from equal averaging to data-size weighting.

E1.justification: The CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet datasets and existing non-IID scenarios remain. V2 adds a bounded new scenario within CIFAR-10: training initially on classes 0–7, then admitting clients with previously unseen classes 8–9 (Appendix A.6). This extends coverage to novel-class arrival without adding another dataset or domain.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds evaluated SparsyFed and Flash comparisons on CIFAR-10/100 Dirichlet partitions. FedPM is added to the CIFAR-100 comparison, including Figure 2(b), while its CIFAR-10 pathological result from v1 Table 1 is omitted. FedAvg and Random also gain entries in corresponding benchmark tables. These substantially expand and revise the actual comparator set.

E3.justification: V2 introduces ResNet-50 evaluation across 50–95% sparsity, an oracle-mask comparison using 1–400 minibatches, and a warmup control with 10 dense rounds evaluated at the same total 500 rounds. Its OOD protocol introduces held-out-class clients at round 225. These are substantial new evaluation designs; the original benchmark partition parameters and core training hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses testing minibatch sufficiency against a full-training-set oracle, sensitivity to initialization versus dense warmup, and adaptation after distribution shift. The earlier permutation, global/local random-mask, longer-training and heterogeneous-client analyses are largely retained or rearranged. However, v1 Appendix A.3's separate saliency-based local-mask experiment reporting 70.22% accuracy is removed.

E5.justification: V1's main accuracy tables contain point estimates. V2 adds explicit five-run reporting, ± quantities in Tables 1–2, random-seed information, and error bars or standard-deviation bands in mask analyses. TinyImageNet FOMO is identified as a single run that failed to converge. V1 already reported uncertainty for communication times. The new run-count disclosures do not establish that more runs were performed than in v1.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results for ResNet-50, oracle-mask estimation, warmup and OOD adaptation; Table 3 reports 47.53% for SSFL versus 12.04% for DisPFL at 95% sparsity. Original headline SSFL benchmark accuracies remain unchanged. FedPM's reported CIFAR-10 Dirichlet accuracy changes from 57.30% to 46.44%, and SubFedAvg's CIFAR-10 communication figure changes from 278.8 to 346.6 MB. Deployment timing values are also revised, rather than merely replotted.

T1.justification: The connection-saliency derivation remains mathematically equivalent despite substantial rewriting. V2 Appendices A.3–A.4 add computational-complexity and communication-cost derivations, including fixed-mask 4sP-byte transmission versus 8sP for COO and 4sP+P/8 for bitmasks. This is a limited analytical extension; the new oracle-mask convergence evidence is empirical, not a convergence proof.

C1.justification: The original contribution of communication-efficient training with a shared initialization-time mask remains. V2 expands its main contributions to near-oracle mask recovery with sufficient client participation, larger-model scalability, and adaptation to unseen classes through a mask refresh. These additions in the introduction and conclusion extend the claimed capabilities beyond v1's static-setting contribution.

C2.justification: V2 develops structural alignment as a stronger explanation for shared-mask performance, adds minibatch-sufficiency and warmup/client-drift interpretations, and extensively argues for hardware-acceleration compatibility. Its new limitations section identifies continuous concept drift as a boundary requiring further adaptation. These materially extend v1's more tentative local-mask drift discussion and existing interpretation of permutation results.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access link, the K=100 benchmark-client count, layer-specific Kaiming initialization details, explicit communication-accounting assumptions, and baseline adaptation information. Most optimizer, epoch, learning-rate, batch-size and partition details were already provided in v1 Appendix A.3. Conversely, v1's named COINSTAC deployment description and explicit deployment architecture list are no longer documented. These are targeted reproducibility changes.

R1.justification: V2 substantially updates positioning around dynamic, structured and initialization-pruning FL, discussing additional work such as SparsyFed, FedPaI and HeteroFL. Appendix B retains much of v1's historical survey while expanding sparse language-model coverage and acknowledging earlier related gradient-aggregation and neuroimaging work. This goes well beyond relocating references or updating bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: The introduction, contribution list, method exposition and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The standalone preliminaries section disappears, much of the original related work moves to Appendix B, and experiments are reorganized into explicit benchmark and analysis subsections. The title and publication formatting also change. The narrative restructuring is substantial independently of added scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 1, reorganizes the original dataset tables into partition-based tables, and replaces the communication-time table with a model-size plot. Existing convergence plots are merged, and client-performance plots move into a composite main-text figure. New oracle/OOD plots and ResNet-50, warmup and cost-analysis tables substantially change the visual presentation beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V1 provided little direct validation of minibatch sufficiency or the decision to avoid warmup, and omitted run counts for benchmark accuracies. V2 substantially addresses these gaps through oracle-mask and warmup experiments, uncertainty reporting, and broader baseline and larger-model comparisons. These strengthen support for the central design. The gains outweigh shortcomings, including removal of the local-saliency-mask experiment, absence of a no-refresh OOD control, and new numerical inconsistencies such as Table 3's 23.21-point gap being described as 24.39 points in the text.
